tasks.short: Develop assessments and procedures for evaluating learning and its application at work.

steps.what: Agree learning outcomes and intended uses of assessment results.
Collect existing assessments, completion records and learner feedback.
Choose assessment methods, scoring criteria and follow-up measures.
Write assessment items, scoring guidance and evaluation procedures.

loop.input: Approved assessment specification, course materials and procedure template.
loop.output: Draft evaluation procedure with assessment items and source references.
loop.check: Validate required sections and outcome coverage; a subject expert checks accuracy and scoring.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per procedure; unresolved items return to the training specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but writing relevant questions and scoring guidance requires language interpretation.

steps.what: Pilot the assessment and observe confusing questions or impractical scoring.
Calculate pilot results and compare outcomes across assessment items.
Approve the revised procedure and release its controlled version.

tasks.design: An integration gathers evidence from the {LMS} and {DOCS}; a template generator uses a bounded drafting loop to prepare assessment procedures. Deterministic calculations feed a {BI} view, while version approval in {WORKFLOW} controls release to the {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, and writing questions required course knowledge. Existing templates did little to connect outcomes, questions and pilot results.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building connectors, coverage checks and report generators. A bounded model loop can draft from approved source material.
tasks.still_hard: Assessment validity, accessible testing and evidence of workplace transfer remain difficult. Small cohorts limit useful statistical comparisons.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what competent performance means and whether an assessment measures it fairly.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling evidence and formatting procedures to observing pilots and improving assessment quality. Authority to change assessment standards still requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Design assessment items and pilot learning materials.
reach.learn: Assessment validity, item analysis and accessible assessment design.

reach.task: Review assessment barriers and accommodation needs.
reach.learn: Fairness review and how to distinguish learning measures from employment decisions.

evidence.claim: Templates, outcome coverage checks and pilot calculations can use deterministic code; question drafting needs expert review.
The design retains human decisions where assessment results could have significant employment consequences.
Using AI assessments for worker performance or promotion requires separate high-risk classification analysis.

assumptions: The main use is learning evaluation, rather than automatic promotion or dismissal decisions.
The {LMS} exposes assessment records through an approved export or interface.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained; evidence assembly and calculations are more rule-covered than procedure design.
GDPR applies; national rules may require employee or works-council consultation.
unknowns: Which assessment results influence pay, promotion, role allocation or employment status?
Who currently approves assessment standards and procedure releases?
Are outcome identifiers and assessment versions recorded consistently?
What employee consultation and data-access arrangements already exist?
research_questions: Which assessment validation methods suit the expected cohort sizes?
What national consultation requirements apply to the proposed assessment use?
Which configured features in the existing {LMS} can replace custom development?
new_work: Review generated questions, scoring guidance and source references.
Investigate misleading pilot results and accessibility problems.
Maintain outcome mappings, templates and integration permissions.
Check retention and access controls for assessment data.

tasks.short: Arrange and deliver continuing technical training and personal development classes.

steps.what: Review training requests, required certifications and employee availability.
Agree course priorities, target groups and delivery format with line managers.
Book approved external provision and authorize the purchase commitment.
Prepare exercises, examples and session guidance for the selected cohort.

loop.input: Approved course materials, learning outcomes and cohort requirements without unnecessary personal data.
loop.output: Draft session pack with exercises and facilitator guidance.
loop.check: Check source references and required sections; the trainer verifies accuracy, accessibility and suitability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per session pack; unsupported technical content returns to the trainer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can assemble materials, but adapting examples and exercises requires language generation.

steps.what: Schedule sessions, rooms and trainer availability.
Enrol employees and issue joining instructions.
Deliver instruction, facilitate practice and respond to learners.
Record verified attendance and assessment outcomes, then request feedback.

tasks.design: Connect approved training needs from the {HCM} and {LMS}, then configure scheduling, enrolment and verified completion updates in the {LMS} and {CALENDAR}. A bounded generator prepares session packs in {DOCS}; purchase approval stays in {PROCUREMENT}, and trainers deliver the sessions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Roster changes, bookings and attendance crossed several systems. Cohort-specific preparation and delivery still needed a trainer.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment and notification features can handle much of the administration. Faster connector development and bounded drafting reduce the remaining preparation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Shift coverage, cancellations, accessibility needs and practical skills teaching remain costly. Attendance alone does not demonstrate competence.
tasks.human_edge: Trainers notice confusion, adapt practice and create the trust needed for honest questions.

ambition.what: Recurring technical training cohorts for shift workers

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time observing teaching and arranging access for underserved groups. Budget and staffing decision rights do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Connect development requests with employee lifecycle events.
reach.learn: Role-based eligibility rules, minimal data sharing and roster quality.

reach.task: Adapt learning exercises and support facilitators.
reach.learn: Adult learning, accessible materials and facilitation for mixed experience levels.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, enrolment, reminders and verified completion updates are suitable for configured workflows.
The digest reports 2.8% hours saved across 11 occupations including HR; this does not establish training-manager savings.

assumptions: The {LMS} supports scheduled sessions, enrolment rules and completion imports.
A approved course plan identifies the audience before automatic enrolment.
Trainers supply verified assessment outcomes; the workflow does not infer competence from attendance.
Live delivery remains a large time share, consistent with the supplied relationship and meeting priors.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies; national rules may require consultation for changes to employee-data processing or monitoring.
unknowns: Which scheduling and notification features are already licensed and configured?
How are shift availability and release from operational duties recorded?
Which courses require observed practice or external certification?
Who can approve provider bookings and cohort priorities?
Which access and consultation processes apply?
research_questions: Can native configuration cover scheduling without custom optimization?
Which delivery formats improve access for shift workers without reducing practice time?
What national rules apply to mandatory training time and employee consultation?
new_work: Review generated session packs and technical examples.
Handle cancellations, missing attendance and roster mismatches.
Maintain enrolment rules, course ownership and connector access.
Check that reminders and enrolment do not disclose unnecessary employee information.

tasks.short: Evaluate training and apprenticeship programs against applicable government standards.

steps.what: Retrieve current official standards and record their versions.
Determine applicable requirements, exemptions and acceptable evidence.
Assemble curricula, instructor qualifications, attendance and assessment evidence.
Compare narrative evidence with requirements and document apparent gaps.

loop.input: Human-approved requirements matrix and versioned program evidence pack.
loop.output: Requirement-to-evidence table with citations, apparent gaps and explicit unknowns.
loop.check: Validate document references and requirement coverage; the reviewer checks each proposed conclusion.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction per program; missing or conflicting evidence is marked unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative curricula and instructor evidence rarely use the same wording as official requirements.

steps.what: Check required hours, dates, qualifications and record completeness.
Discuss gaps with program owners and agree corrective actions.
Sign the compliance review and record conditions for continued operation.

tasks.design: A versioned requirements register in {WORKFLOW} links official material from the {GOV_PORTAL} to evidence from the {LMS} and {DOCS}. Deterministic checks test structured requirements, a bounded loop drafts cited narrative comparisons, and the compliance manager approves the review before corrective actions are tracked in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements and evidence used different formats, and applicable standards needed expert interpretation. Manual evidence gathering was repeated for each review.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors, version checks and requirement tables can now be built with less development effort. Bounded document comparison can prepare traceable reviews without making the legal conclusion.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability, exemptions and whether evidence proves compliance remain expert decisions. Official source access and evidence quality can limit automation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager challenges weak evidence and decides when an apparent gap requires specialist advice or program changes.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting records and more time resolving gaps before programs launch. Compliance sign-off and authority to suspend programs remain with designated decision makers.

reach.task: Maintain apprenticeship agreements and employee eligibility records.
reach.learn: Evidence requirements, document versioning and apprenticeship eligibility.

reach.task: Advise on employee consultation when training arrangements change.
reach.learn: Applicable national rules and the distinction between program review and employee monitoring.

evidence.claim: Versioned evidence registers and checks of explicit hours, dates and qualifications are deterministic design patterns.
Narrative evidence matching can prepare a review, but cannot establish legal applicability or certify compliance.

assumptions: Official standards are available from approved sources with stable retrieval methods.
A compliance specialist approves the requirements matrix before automated checks run.
The task ends with an internal review; government filing is a separate workflow.
The document-heavy prior is retained, with more time assigned to documented applicability than to meetings.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to learner records; apprenticeship and consultation requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Which countries, qualifications and apprenticeship schemes are covered?
Are current standards and evidence available electronically?
Who has authority to sign reviews or restrict program operation?
What evidence retention periods and access permissions are approved?
Which employee or works-council consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which official sources offer dependable change notices or versioned downloads?
What national requirements define acceptable apprenticeship evidence?
Which requirements can be expressed as explicit checks without legal interpretation?
new_work: Maintain approved requirements and source versions.
Review cited narrative comparisons and unresolved evidence.
Investigate failed checks and incomplete records.
Test rules after standards change and track corrective actions.

tasks.short: Align internal courses with regional education providers and define training pathways and procedures.

steps.what: Collect provider course outlines, prerequisites, dates and qualification details.

loop.input: Provider course outlines and timetables received through approved channels.
loop.output: Course records with prerequisites, dates, qualifications and source references.
loop.check: Validate fields and dates; the coordinator checks ambiguous prerequisites and credential claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per document; ambiguous fields remain blank for manual confirmation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Providers supply differently worded documents; structured imports should replace the loop where available.

steps.what: Compare provider courses with internal outcomes, prerequisites and timetable constraints.
Discuss course fit, recognition, learner support and delivery arrangements with providers.
Draft sequencing, attendance, assessment and support procedures.

loop.input: Proposed pathway, confirmed provider terms and approved internal procedure template.
loop.output: Draft training procedure showing sequence, responsibilities and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required sections; the specialist verifies that recognition and support terms match confirmed agreements.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per pathway; unresolved commitments return to the training manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot fully express negotiated responsibilities and differences between internal and provider practices.

steps.what: Approve the pathway and designate its training procedures.
Confirm places and purchasing commitments with the provider.
Publish the agreed pathway and enrolment instructions to employees.
Record approved course mappings, prerequisites and procedure links.

tasks.design: A course register in the {LMS} stores provider offerings and approved mappings; deterministic comparisons show prerequisites and timetable conflicts. Bounded loops extract inconsistent provider documents and draft procedures in {DOCS}, while configured flows in {PROCUREMENT} and {WORKFLOW} manage approved bookings and publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Provider information arrived in inconsistent documents, and course recognition depended on negotiation. Small volumes made bespoke integration difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: A reusable register and document importer are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Existing approval and notification features handle the administration after agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Credit recognition, provider capacity, learner support and release from work remain negotiated matters. Low annual volume may still make configuration the best investment.
tasks.human_edge: The manager builds provider relationships and judges whether a pathway will work for actual learners.

ambition.what: Vocational qualification pathways for employees without formal qualifications

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time discussing pathway quality and learner support, with less document copying. Authority to commit spending or recognize qualifications still requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Map internal learning outcomes to external course requirements.
reach.learn: Qualification frameworks, prerequisite mapping and recognition of prior learning.

reach.task: Assess how funded education fits development benefits.
reach.learn: Education funding rules, repayment terms and applicable national rules.

evidence.claim: Course registers, prerequisite comparisons and approved booking flows can use configuration and deterministic code.
Provider negotiations and qualification recognition remain human decisions; bounded loops can prepare their documents.

assumptions: Regional vocational or professional education providers are the typical European equivalent of community schools.
Providers offer documents or structured catalogues that may be reused with permission.
Comparisons use explicit prerequisites and approved outcome mappings, without automatic claims of qualification equivalence.
The human-class prior remains appropriate for relationship work; preparation and administration can still change.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to learner information; national rules govern funding, employment terms and consultation.
unknowns: Which providers and qualification pathways are already used?
Are course equivalencies formally recognized or only internal recommendations?
Who approves spending, qualification recognition and learner support?
Which employees lack access to existing pathways?
What access permissions and consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Which regional qualification frameworks support recognition of prior learning?
Can provider catalogues be imported through structured interfaces?
What national funding and employment rules apply to the proposed pathways?
new_work: Check extracted provider terms and maintain catalogue versions.
Review drafted procedures and confirm unresolved provider commitments.
Maintain approved mappings and handle timetable exceptions.
Monitor whether new pathways deliver useful qualifications and adequate learner support.

role.altitude: The week shifts toward teaching quality, assessment validity, provider relationships and early resolution of compliance gaps. Administrative capacity increases; spending, employment and compliance decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Training and development specialist: assessment design and qualification mapping.
Human resources specialist: development needs and apprenticeship evidence.
Labor relations specialist: consultation for changes to training and employee-data use.
Equal opportunity officer: accessible assessment and fair access to learning.
skills_to_grow: Workflow design, data quality and exception handling.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring learning pathway review that combines course effectiveness, compliance readiness and access for shift workers and employees without formal qualifications.
